problem: Robots need scene representations that are robust (to camera calibration drift), generalizable across domains, and scalable to large environments, plus LLM-based reasoning that handles 3D spatial relations, mapping and long-horizon state tracking; prior geometry-heavy or purely 2D/LLM approaches fall short on these.
motivation: Embodied agents must perceive and act in 3D from 2D sensors and natural-language instructions. Hand-engineered geometric biases limit robustness and generalization, while LLMs/VLMs remain weak at geometry, arithmetic, navigation memory and state tracking, so the thesis studies both the right scene representation and the right task representation.
key_idea: Combine learnable implicit 3D scene representations (self-calibration, depth fields, NeRF fusion) with LLM spatial reasoning through explicit structure (text-transcribed 3D scenes with code execution, explicit maintained world state), arguing 3D is a complement to large 2D models.
insight: Explicit intermediate structure (a transcribed object list, a tracked world state) lets LLMs succeed where end-to-end reasoning fails. Statler's ablation without state gets 0% episode success on all three domains, and temporal-query success rises from 31% to 83% on pick-and-place. In DeFiNe, removing 3D augmentations or virtual cameras degrades depth, and camera information is critical (Abs.Rel 0.229 without it vs 0.093). Transcrib3D shows text plus code interpretation beats multimodal cross-attention methods, and hints that scarce 3D data is the bottleneck.
method: Self-calibration (Sec 2.1): learns per-sequence intrinsics of unified camera models (UCM/EUCM/DS, closed-form differentiable projection) end-to-end through a self-supervised depth/pose view-synthesis loss; gives sub-pixel reprojection error and can recalibrate from perturbed initializations.

DeFiNe (Sec 2.2): a transformer-based implicit depth field network that ingests multi-view images and camera information, trained with 3D augmentations (virtual cameras, canonical jittering/randomization) and view synthesis as an auxiliary task, for zero-shot generalization.
NeRFuser (Sec 2.3): registers independently trained NeRFs (including relative scale) and blends their renderings via IDW-Sample blending, scaling NeRF to building and city scale.
MANGO (Sec 3.1): a benchmark from text-based games testing LLM mapping and navigation, showing large gaps versus humans (details omitted from the provided text).

Transcrib3D (Sec 3.2): Mask3D detection is transcribed into an object-centric text list, filtered for relevance to the utterance, then a GPT LLM reasons iteratively with a Python interpreter, guided by principles prompting or fine-tuned on self-corrected reasoning.

Statler (Sec 3.3): a world-state reader LLM generates code conditioned on an estimated state, and a world-state writer LLM updates the state after each action, extending Code-as-Policies to a model-based setting.

setting.backbone: Mixed across chapters: CNN depth/pose nets with camera models; DeFiNe transformer; NeRFs; GPT-3.5/GPT-4 (Transcrib3D, Statler; frozen prompted or fine-tuned gpt-3.5-turbo)
setting.training_data: Self-supervised video (KITTI, EuRoC); ScanNet for DeFiNe; NeRFuser per-scene NeRFs; Transcrib3D zero-shot with optional fine-tuning on 500 NR3D training samples; Statler few-shot prompts
setting.observation: Monocular RGB video, RGB-D/colored point clouds, and text descriptions of scenes
setting.action_space: Not navigation-focused; pick-and-place primitive code calls for tabletop manipulation
setting.simulator: Simulated tabletop manipulation domains; no navigation simulator
setting.privileged: Transcrib3D ScanRefer uses GT bounding boxes in some settings; ReferIt3D provides GT segmented objects; otherwise none

numbers_note: The thesis reports no results on the canonical embodied-navigation benchmarks (MANGO's text-navigation results are in the omitted middle). Its results (depth on KITTI/EuRoC/ScanNet, NeRF blending, ReferIt3D/ScanRefer grounding, Statler success rates) are not in the canonical list.
results: Self-calibration reaches sub-pixel reprojection error (EUCM learned 0.245 vs Basalt 0.144) and improves EuRoC Abs Rel to 0.278 vs 0.303 for NRS. DeFiNe gets Abs.Rel 0.100 on zero-shot 7-Scenes vs 0.118 for EST. Transcrib3D (GPT-4 with principles) gets 70.2 on Nr3D and 98.4 on Sr3D vs 64.4 and 76.4 for the best baselines (ViL3DRel, 3D-VisTA). Statler reaches 50%/40%/55% episode success vs 0% for CaP.
limitations: Transcrib3D is object-centric and depends on the quality of 3D detectors and hand-specified features; Nr3D variants were evaluated on 500-sample subsets.
Statler inherits LLM hallucination and weak arithmetic, with modest absolute episode success (40-55%) and small evaluation sets (20 episodes).
Implicit representations are not yet clearly superior to classical SLAM, and global camera models cannot capture local distortion.
